chunks: Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Ibn Miskān, from Abī Baṣīr, who said:

The hadd of the Jew, the Christian, and the slave regarding wine and false accusation is the same. The People of the Covenant were only accorded settlement on the condition that they drink it in their homes.

key_terms.أَهْلُ الذِّمَّةِ: non-Muslim protected subjects living under covenant
key_terms.النَّصْرَانِيِّ: a Christian subject here to the stated legal ruling
key_terms.الْمَمْلُوكِ: a slave or owned servant under the same ruling mentioned
key_terms.الْيَهُودِيِّ: a Jew subject here to the stated legal ruling
key_terms.فِي بُيُوتِهِمْ: within their homes, indicating the restricted place mentioned

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the hadd for Jews, Christians, and slaves in cases involving wine and false accusation?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the legal punishment concerning wine and false accusation applies equally to a Jew, a Christian, and a slave. It also clarifies that Ahl al-Dhimmah were only permitted to drink wine within their own homes, indicating a restricted legal accommodation under covenant.
